segments.text: The History of Exploration
The history of exploration is also the history of humanity
Being drawn toward places not yet seen
At the end of the 15th century, Columbus crossed the Atlantic
And reached the Americas
In the 16th century
The fleet of Magellan achieved
The first circumnavigation of the world
Many sailors lost their lives
But their voyage rewrote the map of the world
In the 20th century
The stage of exploration shifted to the poles
The highest mountains, the deep sea and the sky
In 1911, a munson of Norway
Was the first to reach the South Pole
About a month later, the British team of Scott arrived
But all perished on their return
It was a story of endurance and sacrifice
In a harsh environment
In 1953, Edmund Hillary
And Tenzing Norgay became the first
To stand on the summit of Everest
Their determination showed how strong the human spirit could be
Against the most difficult obstacles
The expedition of Ernest Shackleton
Is another story still told today
His ship was trapped in ice with no rescue in sight
Yet he brought every member of his crew back alive
It was leadership and courage pushed to the extreme today
Exploration heads toward the deep sea
Outer space
And the limits of the human body
Why do people try to cross the boundary?
Perhaps because the question itself
What lies beyond
Is what makes us human
